APCTT-C01.quote: Turbidity and E. coli relations have been used in this way in many other studies, including Lawrence (2012), Brady and others (2009), and Brady and Plona (2012).

APCTT-C02.quote: The purpose of this report is to document the collection and analysis of water-quality parameters and E. coli concentrations in NERI and to develop a near-real-time surrogate model to estimate E. coli concentrations and provide timely information to National Park staff and visitors about the risks associated with using the New River recreationally.
APCTT-C02.note: Intended application for park staff and visitors.

APCTT-C03.quote: For the E. coli recreational-contact standard of 320 MPN/100 mL, the antecedent mean 24-hour turbidity at Thurmond would be estimated by the surrogate model at 23.6 FNU, with a 95-percent confidence interval estimate of 19.4–30.7 FNU.
APCTT-C03.note: Analytical results of the regression model.

APCTT-C04.note: Laboratory analysis of water samples is data collection, not testing of the model.

APCTT-C05.quote: Residuals (fig. 11) had a standard error of 0.469 and were skewed toward lower values but still passed the Shapiro-Wilk’s test for normality with a p-value of 0.0998 (normality p-value greater than 0.05 for this test).
APCTT-C05.note: Model developed and checked against field samples from the river itself; estimated vs measured concentrations (fig. 13, p35).

APCTT-C06.quote: This time-series plot of the surrogate model also indicates that exceedances of the recreational-contact standard were infrequent, with antecedent mean 24-hour turbidity exceeding the 23.6 FNU threshold about 18 times during this 2-year period.
APCTT-C06.note: Borderline: the model was run over the 2-year continuous record at Thurmond.

APCTT-C07.note: The model 'could help' staff; no operational use is reported (p33 discusses future near-real-time use).

APCTT-C10.quote: Residuals (fig. 11) had a standard error of 0.469 and were skewed toward lower values but still passed the Shapiro-Wilk’s test for normality with a p-value of 0.0998 (normality p-value greater than 0.05 for this test).
APCTT-C10.note: A stated acceptance criterion (p > 0.05) and whether it was met. Exceedances of the E. coli standard are water quality, not model performance.

APCTT-C11.quote: Concentrations of Escherichia coli, a species of fecal-coliform bacteria, were monitored in the New River and selected tributaries from October 2021 through September 2023, with emphasis placed on the primary recreational-contact season from May through October.
APCTT-C11.note: Sampling period, monitoring locations and protocols.

APCTT-C12.quote: This surrogate model could help New River Gorge National Park and Preserve staff provide near-real-time information about E. coli concentrations and related recreational-contact risks to the public.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the New River turbidity-based E. coli surrogate model.

notes: Organizer estimate TRL 5; C06 is borderline (model run over the record, not deployed), so this labeller's opinion is TRL 6, low confidence. Module issue: page 39 holds summary text before the References heading but is tagged references.
